metas.name: Gold Diggers of '49
metas.description: Porky and Beans are prospectors during the Gold Rush. When a villain steals Porky's bag of loot, Beans races to get it back so he can marry Porky's daughter Little Kitty.

metas.name: Plane Dippy
metas.description: Porky Pig joins the Army Air Corps. After overcoming the problems caused by his small stature and surviving the rigors of basic training...

metas.name: Page Miss Glory
metas.description: While the rural town of Hicksville anticipates the arrival of one Miss Glory, the bellhop at her modest hotel falls asleep and dreams of paging her at a luxurious metropolitan high rise hotel.

metas.name: The Blow Out
metas.description: A crazed bomber is terrorizing the city. Meanwhile, a young Porky Pig is a few cents shy of buying an ice cream soda; he starts earning it by picking up items people drop and handing them back to them.

metas.name: I'd Love to Take Orders from You
metas.description: Quitting time for a scarecrow. He gets home, and his little boy scares him. To the title song, he teaches his son the basics of scare-crowing. Bedtime for junior; he prays to be a big scarecrow, just like his daddy. The next morning he sneaks out before anyone else is up and practices scaring a roos

metas.name: I Love to Singa
metas.description: A stern classical music teacher becomes a father of four musically-inclined sons, but when one of them demonstrates a preference for jazz music, his father kicks him out of the house.

metas.name: Porky the Rain-Maker
metas.description: The farm is suffering through a terrible drought. Porky's father sends him to the store to buy some feed with their last dollar...

metas.name: Milk and Money
metas.description: Porky's father is going to lose his farm. Porky goes to town with his horse and works a milk route, with a warning that if he breaks a bottle he's fired. As he's delivering, cats follow along behind draining the bottles. Meanwhile, Hank Horsefly follows them into town. He stings Dobbin, who crashes

metas.name: Don't Look Now
metas.description: It's St. Valentine's Day. Cupid is having fun arranging, while a young devil is making mischief sabotaging, love affairs.

metas.name: The Village Smithy
metas.description: The narrator sets the scene for a warped version of the classic poem, and the hijinks when assistant Porky gives the blacksmith a rubber horseshoe, then a hot horseshoe on the horse's backside by accident.

metas.name: Porky the Wrestler
metas.description: Porky Pig, hitchhiking to the big wrestling match, gets a ride from the challenger and unexpectedly winds up also in the ring.

metas.name: Picador Porky
metas.description: Porky and two pals stumble onto a Mexican town on the day of the town's annual bullfight. When they learn the contest winner gets $1,000...

metas.name: I Only Have Eyes for You
metas.description: The iceman is in love with a pretty girl, and an old spinster is pining and cooking for him. But his dreamgirl prefers crooners like Bing Crosby, Rudy Vallee, or Eddie Cantor. After leaving her, he spots the sign of an imitator, and thinks he could ask him to do the crooning for him while he is tryi

metas.name: Porky's Duck Hunt
metas.description: Inexperienced duck hunter Porky Pig is taunted by a mischievous duck (Daffy, making his screen debut).

metas.name: Ain't We Got Fun
metas.description: The cat's asleep, so the mice are on the loose, for a while at least, in the pantry. When he wakes up, they pile the food on him and get him thrown out, and then they *really* have the run of the house.

metas.name: Uncle Tom's Bungalow
metas.description: Warner Bros. cartoon parody of Uncle Tom's Cabin.  One of the “Censored 11” banned from TV syndication by United Artists in 1968 for racist stereotyping.

metas.name: Egghead Rides Again
metas.description: City dweller Egghead dreams of being a cowboy, but his bouncing around gets him kicked out of his boarding house. He sees an ad for a ranch looking for a cowboy and applies. His tryout includes tests of marksmanship and use of a branding iron, but most of it consist of chasing down and roping a trou

metas.name: A Sunbonnet Blue
metas.description: A rat comes between two mice in love.

metas.name: Porky's Garden
metas.description: Porky decides to start a garden. Mayhem ensues.

metas.name: I Wanna Be a Sailor
metas.description: Momma parrot is teaching her young-uns to say "Polly want a cracker" but little Peter doesn't want a cracker, he wants to be a sailor like dad. Mom tells him what a no-account his dad really was, setting sail for Hawaii ("no, Maw, it was Catalina") right after the kids were born. Peter is unswayed,

metas.name: Little Red Walking Hood
metas.description: Red walks past a pool hall; the wolf sees her and pursues her, but, she is oblivious to his come-ons.

metas.name: Daffy Duck & Egghead
metas.description: Daffy taunts a hunter in Tex Avery's classic, meta short.

metas.name: The Sneezing Weasel
metas.description: When Mama hen takes her chicks out to get breakfast, little Wilbur is soaked in a sudden rainstorm and comes down with a head cold. Mama puts him to bed, then goes back out to get the doctor. A conniving weasel, seeing Mama leave, disguises himself as a doctor and comes calling on the unattended chi

metas.name: The Penguin Parade
metas.description: An evening at a night club for penguins, (and a walrus or two). The stage show includes an appearance by a penguin incarnation of Bing Crosby, who sings a jazzy version of, "When my dreamboat comes home". The band's three singers do a scat version as well. This is followed by a full swing band instr

metas.name: The Isle of Pingo Pongo
metas.description: A travelogue spotlights the tropical island of Pingo Pongo, showing the unusual flora and fauna and the lives of the happy natives. One of the “Censored 11” banned from TV syndication by United Artists in 1968 for racist stereotyping.

metas.name: Cinderella Meets Fella
metas.description: Cinderella goes to the ball, where she meets Prince Charming (Egghead).

metas.name: A Feud There Was
metas.description: The McCoys and the Weavers are two feuding hillbilly clans. Elmer Fudd, Peacemaker, attempts to end the fighting; but violence and zaniness win out.

metas.name: Johnny Smith and Poker-Huntas
metas.description: Johnny Smith enters an America where the Indians behave like 1930s average Americans. When he is arrested, the girl Poker Huntas rescues and elopes with him.

metas.name: Daffy Duck in Hollywood
metas.description: Daffy Duck causes trouble on a Hollywood film set.

metas.name: The Mice Will Play
metas.description: The mice are on the loose after hours in a doctor's office, playing with the various pieces of medical apparatus. Susie Mouse is caged for research until her lover Johnnie frees her. A mouse orchestra plays a swinging wedding song. But throughout, a cat is stalking...

metas.name: Hamateur Night
metas.description: It's amateur night at the local theatre, and a procession of bad acts comes and goes: various musicians, a magician, and some actors. But they keep getting interrupted by Egghead singing "She'll Be Comin' 'Round the Mountain".

metas.name: A Day at the Zoo
metas.description: A tour of the zoo, in typical Tex Avery style: a series of one-liners and sight gags, punctuated by Egghead teasing a lion at intervals, despite the admonishments of the narrator.

metas.name: Thugs with Dirty Mugs
metas.description: Killer Diller and his gang are robbing every bank in town in numerical order (except the 13th National Bank, which they skip out of superstition). Despite their predictable actions, the police are unable to catch them...until they get a tip from an unlikely source.

metas.name: Believe It or Else
metas.description: In this Ripley's Believe It or Not! parody, some of the supposed curiosities we are shown are a man who daily drinks fifty quarts of milk, the world's loudest hog caller, a human basketball, a new giant telescope showing life on Mars, and a man who saws people in half.

metas.name: Dangerous Dan McFoo
metas.description: An arctic saloon. The tiny dog, Dan McFoo, is playing a pinball-like marble game in the back. His girlfriend, Sue, sounding like Katharine Hepburn, stands by. A stranger comes in with eyes for Sue; he begins a boxing match with Dan. After Dan gets knocked down, he accuses the stranger of having some

metas.name: Detouring America
metas.description: A humorous travelogue chronicling various oddities across the United States.

metas.name: Land of the Midnight Fun
metas.description: A cruise to Nome, Alaska, starts with some cruise-ship jokes: the ship pulls out of the harbor like a car, raising anchor also raises the front of the boat, the ship follows the coast by curving around it. On arrival, we see some local scenes: A penguin eats two fish, then is eaten by the third; the

metas.name: Fresh Fish
metas.description: A tour of the waters near a South Sea island, introducing us to the various kinds of marine life, including the pickled herring, the hermit crab, the starfish, a seahorse race, and many other puns. Among the running gags, a two-headed fish who keeps asking for directions to Mr. Ripley and a professo

metas.name: Screwball Football
metas.description: A series of gags hung on a football game.

metas.name: The Early Worm Gets the Bird
metas.description: A determined bird goes out early to hunt for a worm and the bird gets into trouble.

metas.name: Cross Country Detours
metas.description: A wacky travelogue takes us to the forests of Yosemite, the rocks of Brice Canyon, the frozen wastes of Alaska, the desert wastes of New Mexico, the Grand Canyon, the Colorado River and the giant redwoods of California.

metas.name: The Bear's Tale
metas.description: The Three Bears meets Little Red Riding Hood, told in the style of Tex Avery.

metas.name: A Gander at Mother Goose
metas.description: A series of gags based on Mother Goose fairy tales and stories.

metas.name: Circus Today
metas.description: A barker guides us through a sideshow, a menagerie, and on to the big top, for a series of typical Avery gags. For example, the trapeze artists, the Flying Cadenzas, literally fly; the lion puts his head in the tamer's mouth; and the human cannonball flies around the world.

metas.name: A Wild Hare
metas.description: While hunting rabbits, Elmer Fudd comes across Bugs Bunny who tricks and harasses him.

metas.name: Ceiling Hero
metas.description: A series of blackout gags parodying aviation and aviation films. Gags include a parchutist whose parachute reads "Good to the last drop", jokes about LA's expanding city limits, and a satire of test pilot and their bravery.

metas.name: Holiday Highlights
metas.description: Blackout gags about the holidays. New Year's (the baby speaks to us). Valentine's Day, Washington Day, etc.

metas.name: Wacky Wildlife
metas.description: A series of typical Avery spot gags set around wild animals. A dainty deer drinks very loudly and rudely from a lake. A pack rat swaps an egg and an acorn, then back again ("monotonous, isn't it?"). A flock of ducks lands; a hunter fires; all fly away, except one with an American flag on its side. A

metas.name: Of Fox and Hounds
metas.description: Willoughby, a big dumb hound, is repeatedly tricked by George, the fox, into jumping off cliffs, among other things.

metas.name: The Haunted Mouse
metas.description: A starving cat wandering in the wilderness sees a sign that says "Ma's Place / Home Cooking / 3 Miles". The cat speeds into town, without noticing the sign that says "Ghost Town / Population 100 Ghosts". One of these ghosts is a mouse eager to get revenge on cats for having tormented him in life.

metas.name: The Crackpot Quail
metas.description: A dog chasing a quail keeps getting outsmarted.

metas.name: Tortoise Beats Hare
metas.description: Bugs Bunny challenges slick Cecil Turtle to a race.

metas.name: Porky's Preview
metas.description: The audience enters Porky's movie theater, with a collection of quick gags: A firefly acting as usher, a kangaroo taking tickets and putting the stubs in her pouch, a chicken buying child tickets for her eggs. A skunk tries to buy a ticket, costing a nickel, but he only has one scent. He looks for a

metas.name: Hollywood Steps Out
metas.description: A tour of Ciro's Nightclub packed with caricatures of many top stars.

metas.name: The Heckling Hare
metas.description: Bugs is being chased by hunting dog Willoughby, and outsmarts him at every turn, until the end, where they outsmart the audience together.

metas.name: Aviation Vacation
metas.description: An animated around-the-world trip by airplane.

metas.name: All This and Rabbit Stew
metas.description: Bugs Bunny heckles a black hunter and escapes from a bear.  One of the “Censored 11” banned from TV syndication by United Artists in 1968 for racist stereotyping.

metas.name: The Bug Parade
metas.description: A spot gag cartoon presenting amusing facts about bugs.
